title: Activity Village MVP Toggle
changes: Added the illustrated Activity Village map as an optional, reversible activity interface.
Added a persistent Settings toggle and an inline Village/Classical view switch.
Added responsive percentage-based hotspots for activity locations.
Added subtle water shimmer, petals, forge smoke, waterfall mist and pond-ripple effects.
Kept the central torii as scenery rather than another duplicated activity menu.
Classic activity cards remain available and use the same progress, unlock and AP state.
Added mobile-friendly scaling, large touch targets and reduced-motion support.
Replaced Practice Grounds with an RPG-style Activity Village.
Added spendable Adventure Points while preserving lifetime XP for leaderboards.
Activities require both enough supported introduced words and enough Adventure Points.
Activity cards show vocabulary readiness, AP cost and restoration status.
Added a full-screen RPG-style building unlock scene with teacher guidance and restoration animation.
Every picture, listening and Karuta pool is strictly limited to introduced supported words.
Picture Meadow starts with an easier Picture + English → Japanese mode.
Unlocked locations become the single place to practise, removing duplicate activity navigation.
Backing out of an activity returns to Activity Village rather than the legacy Games screen.
Redesigned the daily route around Learn → Use → Reinforce.
Main topic progression is always Step 1.
A newly unlocked or relevant activity is Step 2.
Reviews or Memory Warm-up are the final reinforcement step.
Only the current step is actionable and completing it unlocks the next.
Replaced persistent Up next controls with Locked, Start and Complete states.
The main blue action always launches the currently available route step.
Added contextual teacher notifications for newly unlocked activities.
Unlock notices include Start now and Maybe later actions.
Added a short unlock card and teacher avatar animation.
Defined the missing local-storage keys used by social notification dismissals.
Dismissed notifications remain dismissed after refresh and the header icon disappears when none remain.
Friend activity dismissals persist until that friend records newer activity.
Daily review remaining counts now decrease after a planned word is attempted, even when answered incorrectly.
Daily streak qualification is awarded only once per local calendar day.
Three-step route missions are completed as soon as the mandatory session finishes.
The next route step now changes from Up next to Start immediately after the previous mission.
Fixed the dashboard friend-activity dismiss control using persistent delegated event handling.
Fixed popup notification Dismiss so the item disappears immediately and stays read after refresh.
Kept the motivation dismiss button fixed on the right without adding extra lines.
Moved the social notification icon beside the Settings cog.
Fixed the friend activity dismiss button and aligned it on the right.
Fixed Admin Users by reading created_at from auth.users.
Fixed report notifications to use learning_card_reports.status.
Added in-app social notifications and owner report alerts.
Made friend motivation compact and dismissible.
Added friend and invite limits.
Made friend rows clickable with compact unfriend controls.
Added owner-only user listing from leaderboard_entries.
Browser notifications are not included.
Reissued the corrected social release as v9.0.8 for users who already installed v9.0.7.
Removed the GitHub username friend-search form.
Made leaderboard learners selectable with working friend controls.
Added secure one-time friendship links retained through GitHub sign-in.
Invite links expire after 30 days and can only be redeemed once.
Leaderboard learners can now be selected to open a working profile.
Profiles now offer Add friend, Accept, Decline or Unfriend as appropriate.
All Invite and Copy Link actions now generate secure one-time friendship links.
Invitation tokens are retained through GitHub OAuth and redeemed immediately after sign-in.
Invitation links expire after 30 days and can only be redeemed once.
Included the required v9.0.7 Supabase social migration.
Added a first-launch welcome overlay when no Kaishi Quest data exists in local storage.
The overlay highlights Journey, Live Conversation, Japan Ready, the travel cheat sheet, progress tracking and friends.
Added Start exploring and Sign in to save progress actions.
The welcome is dismissed permanently after the learner continues.
Removed all friend-request email functionality.
Made community leaderboard users clickable with profile and friend controls.
New signed-in users join the leaderboard by default and may opt out.
Added secure one-time invite links that automatically connect users after sign-in.
Added a small internal buffer between Journey controls and the green dashboard border.
Reduced Live Conversation to four kana choices.
Wrong kana choices lower the scenario score.
Added friend requests, acceptance, decline and unfriend.
Added recent friend activity encouragement.
Added a dedicated guest learner avatar matching the app’s anime character style.
Made the dashboard GitHub sign-in action clearer and explains cloud progress, cross-device continuation and character selection.
Fixed the Japan Ready Study Modes preview layout on wider desktop browsers.
Expanded all ten Japan Ready scenarios into fuller three-turn practical conversations.
Reworked travel coverage around courtesy, transport, dining, shopping, accommodation, airports and emergencies.
Removed the permanent Recommended Next panel from the Japan Ready page.
The next scenario is now highlighted directly in the scenario list.
Added a sectioned Travel Cheat Sheet with Japanese, romaji, English and phrase audio.
Updated application, data and asset versions to v9.0.5.
Fixed the blank Journey screen from the Study Modes Continue Adventure button.
The Study Modes Journey card now uses the existing working Journey home content and navigation.
Renamed Choose your adventure to Study Modes.
Made the Study Modes card the same width as the rest of the dashboard.
Moved the current topic, teacher recommendation, progress and Journey controls into the Journey mode preview.
Removed the duplicated standalone Journey home section below Study Modes.
Added a matching Japan Ready dashboard preview with Aiko, current scenario, confidence and scenario progress.
Added a smooth transition when switching between Journey and Japan Ready previews.
Updated application and asset versions to v9.0.4.
Added romaji beneath every selectable kana in Live Conversation.
Added romaji beneath kana already placed into the response.
Moved Journey testing, Mnemonic Studio and Image Diagnostics out of normal Settings and into the owner-only Admin area.
Normal Settings now retains only the owner-only Admin entry point.
Updated application and asset versions to v9.0.3.
Redesigned Live Conversation as a WhatsApp-style chat with Aiko on the left and the learner avatar on the right.
Added English translations beneath Japanese NPC and learner messages.
Changed correction wording to A suitable response would be and shows its English meaning.
Plays a correct learner response aloud using a Japanese voice selected to suit the learner avatar.
Journey remains on the dashboard when selected.
Japan Ready highlights only while the Japan Ready screen is active.
Returning from Japan Ready restores Journey as the highlighted dashboard choice.
Updated application and asset versions to v9.0.1.
Added Japan Ready, a focused scenario-based travel campaign.
Added Aiko as the dedicated tourist-guide companion.
Added ten practical travel scenarios.
Added typed Live Conversation with romaji and learned-word suggestions.
Added campaign-specific confidence, completion and unlock tracking.
Shared vocabulary mastery, reviews, XP, streaks, kana, kanji and mnemonics with Journey.
Upgraded cloud snapshot schema to version 3 without resetting existing users.
Added focused scenario study using existing activities.
Updated caching for Japan Ready data and graphics.
Updated application and asset versions to v9.0.0.
Added a versioned service worker that caches common graphics and previously viewed learning images locally.
Preloads mnemonic and built-in images for the next three learning cards.
Limits the runtime image cache to approximately 350 entries.
Keeps version.json network-first so update checks are not trapped by caching.
Added meaningful cloud-state fingerprints to reconcile routine refreshes and tab changes silently.
Automatically keeps the side that changed since the last successful sync.
Ignores Supabase token-refresh events for progress initialisation.
Flushes progress when the page becomes hidden.
Keeps the progress-choice dialog for genuine conflicts and manual Sync or restore.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.3.3.
Capped normal adaptive learning missions at 15 cards.
Limited each recommended mission to up to three new words and six scheduled reviews.
Added a save point every five cards with Continue mission and Finish for now.
Unfinished missions can be resumed through Continue Adventure later the same day.
Mission completion offers an optional additional short mission.
Removed New words per session, Daily review limit and Active words mixed together from Settings.
Added Quick Settings over active cards so preferences can change without leaving the session.
Opening full Settings during a mission saves the current place.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.3.2.
Fixed completed daily reviews reappearing after refreshing or restoring cloud progress.
Today's assigned review plan is now preserved during a Supabase cloud restore.
A completed answer now triggers an immediate cloud flush as well as the normal local save.
The daily review allocation is not regenerated until the calendar date changes.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.3.1.
Added a Report issue action to learning cards for signed-in GitHub users.
Reports capture the word, topic, activity type, displayed card context, app version and viewport automatically.
Added Japanese, English, audio, mnemonic, graphical, answer-option and other issue categories with a 300-character description.
Added a Supabase RPC that enforces a maximum of three reports per authenticated user per UTC day.
Added duplicate-report protection for the same user, card, activity and category.
Added an owner-only Admin area accessible from Settings.
Moved existing owner Journey controls and Mnemonic Studio access into the Admin area at runtime.
Added report filtering, review, reopen, fixed and delete controls.
Added CSV export of unreviewed reports with an option to mark exactly the exported reports as reviewed.
Added Supabase Row Level Security so only registered app administrators can read or manage reports.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.3.0.
Removed the Hear the answer control before a learner selects a reading.
Incorrect reading choices now show a compact teacher correction with the correct Japanese answer.
The correct pronunciation plays automatically once after an incorrect answer.
A speaker control remains in the correction panel so the learner can replay the answer.
The memory hint is removed after an answer is selected.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.2.1.
Added one curated learning graph used by the Journey, Topic Adventure, adaptive sessions, Collection and topic bosses.
Mapped 2,139 unique imported Japanese words across 28 practical topics and 6 regions.
Added reusable foundations for numbers, counters, colours, days and dates, time, question words, directions, people, verbs, descriptions, particles and polite expressions.
Foundation knowledge is introduced at a relevant point and then reused naturally across later topics rather than being trapped in isolated lessons.
Topic sessions can now mix relevant mastered foundation words into the current subject.
Topic bosses assess both the topic itself and the reusable foundations needed in that real situation.
Added a Foundations area to Collection and foundation links on discovered words.
Added topic, foundation and low-confidence mapping reports for ongoing review.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.2.0.
Added a dedicated Japanese school teacher for all mentor, recommendation, boss, story and milestone guidance.
Kept the old Master Sensei character separate as a selectable learner avatar.
Removed the duplicate old-man emoji fallback from guidance notifications.
Fixed the mobile recommendation card so text uses the available horizontal width instead of collapsing into a narrow column.
Character Unlock now clearly previews the exact upcoming vocabulary word that uses the new kana.
The primary Character Unlock action is now Learn [kana] now rather than the misleading Use it in [word] wording.
After the final required kana is learned, the app immediately opens First Encounter for that exact word.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.1.0.
Replaced learner-facing numbered chapters with topic-first Japanese regions.
Added a simplified Home focused on Continue Adventure, reviews, Practice Grounds and Collection.
Added Sensei recommendations to the Home and topic Journey using the existing old-man companion.
Added Practice Grounds as the permanent home for every unlocked game and learning activity.
Added a Collection for discovered words, topics, mnemonic memories and achievements.
The adaptive Journey now prioritises the current topic and selects games based on the weakest skill.
Added topic boss reviews that mix meaning, listening, reading, picture memory, sentences and recall.
Completing a topic boss unlocks the next Japanese region.
Words remain grouped with their assigned topic so learning, games, sentences and boss review reinforce the same subject.
Updated application and asset versions to v8.0.0.
Added Character Unlock, First Encounter and Example Sentence stages to the per-word Journey.
Required Hiragana and Katakana can now be introduced immediately before the vocabulary that needs them.
Added Sensei guidance using the existing old-man companion artwork with an emoji fallback.
Imported 2,143 Anki notes containing Japanese words, meanings, romaji and example sentences.
Added topic-aware vocabulary enrichment and ordering while preserving existing IDs, SRS and learner progress.
Kept mnemonic images and the varied game system at the centre of the learning flow.
Updated application and asset versions to v7.2.0.
Active Recall now removes the built-in vocabulary picture whenever an approved mnemonic image is available.
The Show memory hint button disappears immediately after Reveal answer is selected.
The separate Play audio button has been replaced by a compact speaker icon beside the revealed Japanese word or Kanji.
Reduced clutter in the revealed-answer area while preserving ratings and mnemonic support.
Updated application and asset versions to v6.9.1.
Redesigned Meet the Word cards to combine the Japanese reading and English meaning into one compact row.
The full How to learn this word guidance opens for the first two introductions in a session, then defaults to a compact expandable control.
Removed the duplicate How to learn this word panel created by overlapping app and mnemonic-card enhancements.
Made the Meet the Word continue action sticky at the bottom of the viewport so it remains reachable while the card scrolls.
Condensed per-word Journey guidance into a compact horizontal badge that uses mobile width more efficiently.
Moved Share progress into a small badge beside the three-step route heading.
Changed Why these missions into a collapsed explanation that expands on demand.
Compressed the three Journey mission cards and limited supporting text to two lines.
Kept the current 1,500-word expedition chapter fully expanded while reducing all other chapters to compact two- or three-line summaries.
Updated application and asset versions to v6.9.0.
Meet the Word cards now use an approved mnemonic image instead of also showing the ordinary built-in vocabulary picture.
Added clear labels for the Kanji or written Japanese word, its reading and its English meaning.
Moved the Japanese word audio control beside the written word and reduced it to a clear speaker icon.
Added learner guidance explaining how to connect the mnemonic picture, sound clue, story and meaning.
Mnemonic stories are now shown automatically by default for new users while preserving existing saved preferences.
Updated application, page and asset versions to v6.8.0 so cached browsers receive the new learning card layout.
Added the Particle Shrine Grammar & Particles learning path with sequential particle lessons, spoken examples and in-context questions.
Grammar unlocks on the Journey after 15 started words and 15 tested answers, and remains repeatable from the Practice Hub and Games.
Added 46 new approved mnemonic scenes to reach 646 mapped vocabulary images.
Updated asset versions to v6.7.0 so cached browsers receive the grammar path and new mnemonic images.
Added the Kanji Workshop Journey landmark and a repeatable Kanji Builder game.
Added 105 curated, learner-facing visual component lessons linked automatically to every matching vocabulary word.
Kanji Builder asks learners to assemble components in order from an English meaning and spoken Japanese clue.
Selected components animate into the central construction stage and can be removed before locking in an answer.
Every answer now pauses for the completed Kanji, reading, English meaning, audio, component definitions and memory explanation.
Added interactive component breakdowns to the existing Kanji progress overview and a browsable lesson library.
Added a separate Kanji-components skill score and meaningful-activity credit for completed builder answers.
Clearly distinguishes visual components from official dictionary radicals and historical etymology.
Moved replay subtitles to the upper part of the Theatre stage so they no longer cover the speaking character portraits.
Added responsive subtitle spacing and height limits for narrow mobile screens.
Gave Kai, Mia and Master distinct Japanese voice profiles, with gender-aware voice selection where the browser provides suitable voices.
Added pitch and speaking-rate fallbacks so the three characters remain clearly distinguishable across Windows, mobile and other browsers.
Replaced the Theatre bobbing effect with stable character poses, subtle face-and-shoulder speaking movement and animated voice waves around the active speaker.
Added Kaishi Theatre with eight lightweight animated Japanese scenes featuring Kai, Mia and Master.
Each 13–16 second scene uses Japanese speech, character movement and visual action while keeping first-play subtitles hidden.
Every performance selects two questions at random from five credible comprehension choices.
Completed scenes unlock sequentially and track attempts, completion and personal-best scores.
After the questions, learners can replay with Japanese subtitles and explore every line through readings, natural English, vocabulary chunks, particles and grammar.
Kaishi Theatre joins the guided Journey after one Conversation Quest and remains repeatable in the Practice Hub and Games.
Manga Meaning-to-Japanese questions now hide the source sentence until after the learner answers.
Manga sentence choices now prioritise close, believable distractors instead of unrelated story events.
Every Manga panel answer now reveals the complete Japanese sentence as vocabulary chunks, particles, grammar and natural English.
Conversation answers now break down the character prompt, best response and follow-up reply regardless of whether the answer was correct.
Added an adaptive three-step daily Journey route combining review, the current vocabulary chapter and another learning activity.
Journey missions only complete after a tested answer, then show a useful session summary and the next recommended step.
Newly unlocked activities are introduced by the Journey before appearing in the repeatable Practice Hub.
Added friend invitations through the device share menu, WhatsApp and a copyable link.
Added downloadable square achievement cards for sharing progress through Instagram and other apps.
Removed the Classic dashboard fallback so every learner now follows the Journey experience.
Moved the learner's clickable Kaishi character, username and streak milestone into the Ready to learn hero.
Removed the separate dashboard profile block for a more compact home screen.
Added a complete 30-chapter vocabulary expedition covering all 1,500 words in groups of 50.
Each chapter opens after 40 words are introduced and 25 different words receive tested review practice, without requiring perfect mastery.
Journey vocabulary sessions now draw new words and reviews from the selected chapter.
Separated early activity landmarks from the long-term vocabulary route while keeping unlocked activities freely repeatable.
Added owner-only controls for unlocking through any vocabulary chapter during testing.
Continue Journey now opens the visual learning road at the learner's current landmark before starting an activity.
Activities launched from Journey return to the road instead of sometimes returning to the Games page.
Journey progress now distinguishes early activity unlocks from the longer 1,500-word expedition, shown as 30 vocabulary chapters.
Made Guided Journey the default home experience, with the learner's selected character moving along a responsive activity road.
Added nine permanent learning milestones that unlock from demonstrated vocabulary, listening, Kanji and review progress.
Added a Practice Hub where every unlocked activity can be repeated at any time.
Added a Settings option to restore the complete Classic dashboard without losing journey progress.
Added owner-only @terryjread-sudo controls to unlock through any milestone or reset testing overrides.
Existing learner statistics automatically grant every journey unlock already earned.
Updated asset versions to v6.2.0 so cached browsers receive the new default experience.
Added Conversation Quest with 15 scripted Japanese conversations and 60 contextual response decisions.
Conversation prompts, learner replies and character reactions can be spoken with a Japanese browser voice.
Every response reveals its English meaning, reading, best answer and a brief usage explanation.
Conversations unlock sequentially and include personal bests, transcripts and linked vocabulary summaries.
Added a resumable Conversation Quest recommendation to the dashboard and a dedicated mode inside Games.
Updated asset versions to v6.1.1 so cached browsers receive the latest Manga, Karuta and Conversation changes.
Replaying Karuta audio now keeps the original reaction timer running.
Manga Stories now unlock one at a time after the preceding story is completed.
Manga Story runs now rotate vocabulary, full-sentence meaning, Japanese sentence matching and story-comprehension questions.
Completed the 100-scene mnemonic expansion to reach 600 approved, app-visible vocabulary images.
Added a Manga Stories library with 10 original, graded Japanese reading exercises.
Included 57 manga panels across four difficulty levels, from four-panel beginner stories to an eight-panel challenge.
Placed app vocabulary inside complete Japanese sentences with natural conjugated forms.
Added optional reading reveals, target-word audio and English translations after each attempt.
Added contextual meaning questions and a final comprehension check to every story.
Connected Manga Story answers to vocabulary SRS, meaningful daily streaks and optional cloud progress.
Added per-story completion counts, personal-best scores and an audio story glossary.
Made the Kanji mastered dashboard tile open the complete Kanji progress overview.
Added Japanese labels to the main dashboard navigation buttons.
Moved skill scores to a dedicated page with current strength, accuracy, attempts and tested-word counts.
Replaced the SRS Decay Battle gradient with a responsive illustrated Japanese garden arena.
Daily streaks now require five tested answers from Vocabulary, Kana, Karuta, picture games or SRS battles.
Added a visible daily streak-progress meter so browsing alone cannot protect a streak.
Resequenced new vocabulary into introduction, meaning, listening, reading and optional picture stages.
Delayed production, sentence and Kanji recall until recognition is established.
Mnemonic scenes now fade after sustained recall while remaining available through the hint button.
Added a complete Kanji progress overview with hidden, introduced, practised and mastered states.
Added word-level learning states within each revealed Kanji.
Added separate Words, Kanji and Kana mastered totals to the dashboard.
Added the best Karuta average points per card from the last 72 hours.
Changed the Yōkai activity summary to a rolling 72-hour window.
Changed the due-review circle into a draining progress ring based on today's planned reviews.
Added Karuta, a timed audio-reflex game using learned words with Japanese audio and mnemonic images.
Karuta cards combine the complete mnemonic scene with a clear Japanese word overlay.
Added reaction-time scoring, fast-answer combo multipliers, personal bests and a detailed round summary.
Karuta pauses after every tap to reveal the reading, English meaning and replayable Japanese audio.
Hidden the Mnemonic Studio link unless the authenticated GitHub username is @terryjread-sudo.
Added the same authenticated-owner check to direct Mnemonic Studio page visits.
Kept the Studio interface locked until Supabase confirms the owner account.
Replaced the dashboard character-type label with the signed-in learner's username.
Made the dashboard profile picture open and highlight the character picker in Settings.
Removed the redundant Your streak character heading from the dashboard.
Moved the optional community leaderboard from the dashboard to its own page.
Added a Community challenge button directly below Games.
Made the signed-in learner's leaderboard row clearly identifiable with a profile badge and stronger highlight.
Added five optional Kaishi profile characters for signed-in learners.
Characters unlock thumbs-up, double-thumbs, flexing and superhero portraits at streak milestones.
Displayed the selected streak character on the dashboard and public leaderboard.
Added a seven-day, one-attempt streak rescue after a streak is lost.
The rescue battle requires 10 correct answers with no mistakes and no audio hints.
Added an original friendly Kaidōra kaiju with approach, hurt and defeated battle sprites.
Added a Listen to Meaning game with illustrated English choices.
Games now reveal the Japanese word, reading, English meaning, and replayable audio after every answer.
Learners choose when to move to the next question instead of being advanced automatically.
Removed the Picture to Meaning game.
Added a Kaishi Quest character banner behind the main title bar.
Updated mnemonic image frames to show complete landscape artwork without cropping.
Replaced the rectangular title-bar artwork with a responsive transparent character group.
Updated image diagnostics to display complete landscape mnemonic scenes without cropping.
Updated the title artwork to feature only the main boy, girl, and elderly calligraphy master.
Improved auxiliary-page navigation with high-contrast Back to app badges.
Replaced Picture to Reading with Picture plus Kanji to Meaning.
Added the total vocabulary count beside the Mastered statistic.
Added memory links and reference-guided scene images for 100 more high-frequency words.
Made approved the default image status while preserving explicit regeneration flags.
Made image diagnostics load every mapped scene directly from the scene catalogue.
Added SRS Decay Battles, a tower-defence review mode driven by words near their forgetting threshold.
Correct battle reviews damage and push back monsters; mistakes let them advance toward the castle.
Battle answers still reveal the Japanese word, reading, English meaning, and playable audio.
Added four friendly Japanese yōkai with approaching, hurt, and defeated visual states.
Added responsive monster movement, recoil, defeat animations, and reduced-motion support.
Added optional Japanese audio hints with stronger no-hint critical attacks.
Added a battle summary with accuracy, hints, critical hits, weak words, and dojo health.
Added a rolling dashboard count of yōkai defeated during the last 24 hours.
Added 297 reference-guided mnemonic scenes to reach 500 mapped vocabulary images.
Each new scene combines visible pronunciation props with a memorable meaning action.
Marked every new mnemonic image approved by default for immediate study and game use.
Added optional GitHub sign-in through Supabase while keeping guest play available.
Added private cloud progress backup with cross-device restore and conflict choices.
Added an opt-in community leaderboard that never exposes individual word progress.
Kept manual progress export and local-only play available without an account.
